EV-P2.title: High Voltage Cycling Stability of LiF-Coated NMC811 Electrode
EV-P2.claim: Source values for the P2 hero fixture: 95:3:2, 10.5 mg/cm2, about 2 mAh/cm2, 200 uL, Ar <1 ppm.

EV-P4.title: P4 NMC811 || Li transfer-case source
EV-P4.claim: Source metadata only; no paper text is included.

EV-P5.title: P5 NMC811 || Li transfer-case source
EV-P5.claim: Source metadata only; no paper text is included.

EV-B1.title: Composition and slurry mass balance
EV-B1.claim: m_i = f_i * m_solids; sum(f_i) = 1; solids wt% = m_solids / (m_solids + m_NMP), with NMP density 1.03 g/mL.

EV-B2.title: Areal capacity = active loading x specific capacity
EV-B2.claim: 10 mg/cm2 active x 200 mAh/g = 2.0 mAh/cm2; the /1000 conversion is required.

EV-B3.title: Li areal capacity and excess
EV-B3.claim: Li density 0.534 g/cm3 x 3860 mAh/g = 0.2061 mAh/cm2 per um; ratio = Q_Li / Q_cathode.

EV-B4.title: Electrolyte volume per areal capacity
EV-B4.claim: uL/mAh = V / (Q_areal x electrode area); g/Ah = uL/mAh x 1.26 mg/uL.

EV-B5.title: Salt molarity and mass
EV-B5.source: LiPF6 datasheet and battery reference pack
EV-B5.claim: n = M x V; m_salt = n x MW; mixed-salt total molarity is the sum of salts in the same solution. LiPF6 MW 151.9 g/mol.

EV-C1.title: Water budget and HF upper bound
EV-C1.source: Battery reference pack, formula 5; moisture table
EV-C1.claim: m_H2O = m x ppm / 1e6; m_HF,max = 2.22 x m_H2O; ppm on CAM basis is per CAM mass, not per batch.

EV-C2.title: Atmosphere and drying screen
EV-C2.claim: Li metal requires an Ar glovebox at <=1 ppm H2O/O2; CAM powder 110-130 C, vacuum, >=3 h; coated electrode 80 C, vacuum, >=4 h.

EV-430.title: 430 ppm is a Gr/NMC622 reference, not an NMC811 constant
EV-430.claim: Show 430 ppm as a warning/reference line only; do not use it as a hard NMC811 fail threshold.

EV-HF.title: LiPF6 hydrolysis and HF upper bound
EV-HF.claim: The 2.22 mass ratio is an upper-bound conversion from water to HF-equivalent, not a measurement of free HF.

EV-LI.title: Li metal and Ar glovebox safety
EV-LI.claim: Li metal reacts with N2 and water; use an Ar glovebox with controlled H2O/O2 and follow EHS review.
